_convention: What the sprites ARE, not how they are played. Written from looking at them (npm run sheet); a leading '?' marks a guess to be settled when the move is actually built. A frame may belong to several groups and may appear more than once in one animation (a guard pose is often both the wind-up and the recovery) — say so in its description. Playback order and timing live in animations.json and are NOT recorded here: they cannot be read off a sheet, and a second copy would only go stale.

base_form.desc: Goku before transforming — black hair, calmer poses. Frames 0 and 2 are dithered: a SNES transparency effect, so they are the fade in/out of the transformation rather than real poses. 0 had been detected a pixel narrow (33 wide against 2's 34) because the dithering left its rightmost column too sparse to find; re-cut by hand 2026-08-15 to match 2. Its drawn pixels still stop 4 px above the anchor and 7 px below the top — the dithering eats the hair tips and the feet first — so any box derived from this frame comes out short.

idle.desc: Super Saiyan neutral stance, fists up, weight even. Three near-identical frames that read as breathing.

walk.desc: Two-frame walk cycle, guard held up. Used for BOTH directions — walking backwards plays the same frames, only the velocity differs (walk_fwd / walk_back). Looked at 2026-08-15: THE FEET DO NOT MOVE between 9 and 10 — same wide stance, same foot placement, only the arms and the body height change. It is a bob, not a step, so walking will always read as gliding and no retiming can fix it. The sheet has no walking legs.

jump_up.desc: ? Vertical jump: rise with the body upright and legs extended, then tuck. See the note on 17 — the tucked pair looks like 15/16 rather than 17/15.

jump_fwd.desc: Take-off for the forward jump: airborne, body angled, legs trailing. Continues into air_spin.

air_spin.desc: Airborne somersault, four frames of a full rotation — the loop for a travelling jump. Consecutive on the sheet, which is a good sign the numbering is right.

dash_fwd.desc: Dashing forward, confirmed by the owner 2026-08-15: 24 is the pose the dash starts from, 25 is the dash itself — torso pitched far forward, trailing leg straight out behind, hair blown back. Used to be half of a group called "lunge" that read the four frames as one run cycle; they are two dashes, not a cycle. These and dash_back are the only frames on the sheet where the legs travel at all — the walk does not step.

dash_back.desc: Dashing backwards, confirmed by the owner 2026-08-15: 26 is the start pose and is the same pose as 24, 27 is the backward dash. The start pose appearing twice is the sheet giving each dash its own strip, not two different poses.

powerup.desc: Ki charge: standing with fists clenched low inside a bright aura flare, growing over three frames.

punch_light.desc: Straight punch. 32 is the guard the punch starts from AND the pose it pulls back to, so it appears twice in the animation (32 → 33 → 32); 33 is the extended, active frame. Frames can serve several purposes like this — the catalogue names the pose, the animation decides the order.

crouch_attack.desc: ? Crouched with the lead arm driving forward — an attack from a low stance, but which one is unconfirmed. 47, 49 and 53 used to be lumped in here and turned out to belong to the air kick, the flying kick and the crouching kick.

fx_impact.desc: ? Effect sprites, not poses: a burst of flame that grows and then breaks up. Almost certainly the hit spark for something — which move is unknown. Relevant to the spark spawns in data/spawns/.

overhead_swing.desc: ? A committed overhead attack: guard, swing with a bright arc trail, recovery with the arm still up. Grouping and order are read off the sheet, not confirmed.

hurt.desc: Hit reactions, standing. 74 alone is the light one — a single flinch after something like the light punch. 74 followed by 75 is the heavier one: the same flinch continued into a real recoil, so the two share a first frame rather than being separate animations. 76 is a hit to the stomach / a low blow. Confirmed by the owner.

knockdown.desc: Being put on the floor: 77 is the start of going down (also read as a stun, and as the start of taking damage while airborne), 78 the fall itself, 79 landed and lying, 80 and 81 getting back up. Confirmed by the owner; see docs/plan.md item F.

ki_blast.desc: ? A projectile attack: 54 gathers both hands in front of the chest, 55 thrusts one arm out — the charge and the release. 56-60 are the projectile itself, not poses. Whether this is the Kamehameha or a smaller ki blast is unconfirmed.

kick_basic.desc: The basic kick: 34, 35, 36. Confirmed by the owner. 36 is the extended frame, at hip height.

kick_heavy.desc: The heavy kick: 37, 38, 39. Confirmed by the owner. 39 is the extended frame, the highest of the three kicks.

kick_combo.desc: A kick used inside a combination rather than on its own: 40, 41, 42. Confirmed by the owner. 42 is the extended frame, along the ground.

kick_air.desc: A kick thrown while airborne: 46, 47. Confirmed by the owner.

flying_kick.desc: A special attack from the air, the flying kick: 48, 49. Confirmed by the owner. Not being built yet — specials come after the basic moves.

uppercut.desc: A blow struck upward into the chin: 50, 51. Confirmed by the owner.

kick_crouch.desc: A kick thrown from a crouch: 52, 53. Confirmed by the owner.

guard_stand.desc: ? Upright with the forearms crossed in front of the chest, three near-identical frames. NOT the block — that is 28. What they actually are is unconfirmed.

crouch.desc: The low stance, confirmed by the owner: 17 is the transition down into it, 18 is the neutral crouch held at the bottom. A crouching guard exists in the game but is not on this sheet.

guard.desc: The block, confirmed by the owner: 28. Held as a reaction to a blow that arrives, not as a stance you stand in.

kick_from_depth.desc: An attack that leaves the plane of the fight: Goku jumps into the depth of the screen and comes back out of it with a kick. Confirmed by the owner 2026-08-15. 82 is the launch and 83 the way in — both dithered, the SNES half-transparency standing in for fading out; 84 is the far point; 85 and 86 are the return, leg already extended. Distance is drawn as scale, which is why the frames shrink to 59 px and back. Name is provisional. Watch out: a shrinking silhouette on this sheet does NOT mean a second small-scale sprite set — it means depth inside a move.

ki_blast.desc: Firing a ki bolt, confirmed by the owner 2026-08-15. Goku steps to the FOREGROUND — nearer the camera — to shoot: 87 is the foreground pose (and most likely the frame that carries the step there), 88 is the full-body white flash that starts the attack, 89 the arm wind-up, 90 the shot. Shares 87 and 88 with kamehameha, which is what a shared entry looks like. The foreground is drawn as scale and it is subtle: 83–85 px against the idle's 81–82, so playing the frames gives the effect without the engine scaling anything.

kamehameha_foreground.desc: The Kamehameha fired from the FOREGROUND, confirmed by the owner 2026-08-15. Same entry as ki_blast — 87 in the foreground, 88 the white flash — then 91 charges it and 92 fires. There is a second, plainer Kamehameha on the normal plane (see kamehameha), and that is the one worth building first now that the depth plane is not a mode. Keep the two apart: this one only has a forward shot and cannot exist without the step toward the camera.

recede.desc: Going away into the depth of the screen, confirmed by the owner 2026-08-15. A scale ramp and nothing else: the same standing pose at 67, 54, 37 and finally 30 px, against the idle's 81. This is the transition; everything suffixed _far below is what Goku can do once he is there.

idle_far.desc: Standing in the depth of the screen, ~29 px. 98 is the pose; 100 is nearly the same and may be its second frame or the neutral the deflects return to — unconfirmed. 97 is the whole body flashed white, the far-scale twin of 88.

deflect_far.desc: Batting away ki bolts while in the depth of the screen, confirmed by the owner 2026-08-15: 99 and 101, an arm thrown up and forward in each. Being far is not being safe — it is a different set of options.

dodge_far.desc: Avoiding a blow while in the depth of the screen, confirmed by the owner 2026-08-15: 102 and 103, the body pulled aside.

hurt_far.desc: Taking damage while in the depth of the screen, confirmed by the owner 2026-08-15: 104 recoiling, 105 doubled over. The far plane has its own hit reactions, which is what makes it a second place to fight rather than a pose.

ki_bolt.desc: ? Not poses — the ki projectile itself, drawn at six sizes: 42, 32, 16, 12, 10 and 8 px. Almost certainly distance rather than time, since ki_blast fires from the foreground and the bolt travels away from the camera. If so, which frame is drawn is decided by where the bolt is, not by an animation clock. 116-119 are smaller yellow scraps of the same family and may be its tail or the debris of an impact.

hop_lunge.desc: From the original: Goku hops into a long stride and jumps out of it, confirmed by the owner 2026-08-15. 120 is the wind-up, 121 throws the leg high and starts the stride, 122 is airborne and attacking, 123 comes down in a straddle, 124 lands out of it. The owner notes 121 also stands on its own as a high-leg attack, which is exactly the kind of reuse a state gives us for free. Name is provisional.

teleport.desc: Vanishing, confirmed by the owner 2026-08-15: 125 solid, 126 half dithered, 127 nearly gone — the SNES half-transparency again, here as a teleport rather than a transformation or a step into the background. 127 was detected wrongly (the dithering left holes, so the box was cut to 34x78 and the surviving pixels below it became a bogus frame 128); the box is now 34x93 like 125, anchored at the feet, and 128 is deleted.

kamehameha.desc: The Kamehameha on the normal plane, confirmed by the owner 2026-08-15: 129 charges it with the hands cupped at the hip, 130 fires level, 131 fires upward. Two firing angles is what makes this the version to build rather than kamehameha_foreground. The 72-78 px heights are a deep straddled stance, not a change of scale — the idle is 81.

fx_kamehameha.desc: The beam's own sprites, not poses: 132 and 133 are a half-round segment, 134 and 135 a comet head, 136 a larger burst. Deferred by the owner 2026-08-15 — the move gets built before its effect does.

throw.desc: Taking hold of the opponent and throwing them, confirmed by the owner 2026-08-15: 137 the grab with both hands out, 138 holding and starting the throw, 139 the release — Goku has turned, so the opponent goes behind him. Nothing in our combat design has a throw in it yet; these three frames are the first evidence that one belongs there.

ultimate.desc: The original's ultimate, and the longest sequence on the sheet — confirmed by the owner 2026-08-15. Four movements in one: Goku transforms to SSJ3 (140 start, 141 the hair growing, 142 transformed), throws a jumping uppercut (143 gathers, 144 the uppercut, 145 airborne after it), turns away as SSJ3 wears off (147), then charges and throws a Genki Dama with the hair already back to base form (148 arms up mid-revert, 149 arms up in base form, 150 the throw), and finishes by going Super Saiyan again (151 with the aura, 152 the same pose without it). 146 is not a pose: it is the arc of light left where he was, which in our engine is an fx entity spawned at the departure point rather than a frame of this animation. Worth knowing for the design: every transformation here is transient inside one move, so it needs no engine support at all — a transformation you *stay* in would be another matter entirely.

victory.desc: Winning, confirmed by the owner 2026-08-15: Goku turns to face the screen, drops out of Super Saiyan and stands there scratching his head. 153 is SSJ facing front, 154 the hair reverting, 155 base form facing front, 156 and 157 the hand up behind the head. The whole set faces the camera, which is why none of it is mirrored like the fighting poses.

fx_explosion.desc: ? Effect sprites, not poses: a fireball that swells white-hot and then tears apart — 61 and 62 the growing ball, 64 the peak at 26x26, 63 and 65 breaking up in orange, 66 an arc of debris, 67 the last specks. Sheet order is probably not play order. Neighbours fx_impact (68-70), which is the same family at a smaller size; whether they are one effect or two is unconfirmed.

fx_electric.desc: Electrical discharge, confirmed by the owner 2026-08-15 — nineteen blue-white lightning arcs from 32x26 down to 5x7, the crackle that surrounds a Super Saiyan. Deferred: the owner expects some of these to need their size and position corrected, which is exactly what sparse effect sprites do to auto-detection. Measure before using any of them (see the add-animation skill).

palettes.desc: Not poses: one standing pose recoloured five ways, kept on the sheet as examples of the alternate palettes (confirmed by the owner 2026-08-15, to be dealt with later). Nothing animates these.

frames.9: SSJ walk, guard held. NOT mid-stride: the feet are planted in the same wide stance as 10 (looked at 2026-08-15)
frames.10: SSJ walk, same foot placement as 9 — only the arms rise and the body lifts. The pair is a bob, not a step
frames.11: ? standing guard: upright, forearms crossed in front of the chest, weight even
frames.12: ? standing guard, second frame — near-identical to 11, the pair reads as breathing
frames.13: ? standing guard, third frame — the arms sit fractionally lower than in 11

frames.21: airborne somersault, rotated further, feet uppermost
frames.22: airborne somersault, body horizontal, head to the right
frames.23: airborne somersault, curled, head up and to the left
frames.24: the pose a dash starts from — upright, weight forward, fists up. Same pose as 26
frames.25: dashing forward: torso pitched far forward, trailing leg straight out behind, hair blown back
frames.26: the pose a dash starts from, same as 24 — the sheet gives each dash its own strip
frames.27: dashing backwards, low and pitched, arms leading
frames.28: the block: braced, arms up and across, taking a blow rather than throwing one. Confirmed by the owner
frames.29: SSJ charging: fists clenched low, bright aura flaring around the whole body
frames.30: SSJ charging: same pose, larger aura
frames.31: SSJ charging: same pose, aura at its largest
frames.32: square guard: feet planted, both fists up at chest height — the light punch starts here AND returns here, so it appears twice in that animation
frames.33: straight punch fully extended, lead fist out at shoulder height, body turned into it — the active frame
frames.34: basic kick: standing with both fists up near the shoulders, feet apart, no leg committed yet
frames.35: basic kick: side-on, torso leaning back, lead knee lifted
frames.36: basic kick, the extended frame: lead leg straight forward at hip height, arms up for balance
frames.37: heavy kick, the wind-up: torso leaning back, knee lifted, arms drawn in. Confirmed by the owner
frames.38: heavy kick, the strike being delivered: leaning forward off the back foot with one arm trailing behind. Confirmed by the owner
frames.39: heavy kick, the extended frame: leg extended forward and upward, body leaning well back — the highest of the three kicks
frames.40: combination kick: upright, lead fist forward at chest height, rear fist low
frames.41: combination kick: knees bent, both fists up, compact
frames.42: combination kick, the extended frame: leg extended forward near the ground, body leaning far back — the lowest of the three kicks
frames.43: ? standing tall with one arm swung up overhead, body stretched — an overhead attack of some kind; NOT the uppercut, which is 50/51
frames.44: ? crouched low with the lead arm driving forward
frames.45: ? crouched low, arm extended further forward than 44 — the same attack one frame on
frames.46: air kick: body compact and leaning back, fists up, legs gathered — the frame before the leg goes out
frames.47: air kick, the extended frame: lead leg out low and forward, body leaning back to counterbalance
frames.48: flying kick (special, not built yet): body tucked tight, arms in front — the launch of a committed airborne charge
frames.49: flying kick (special, not built yet), the extended frame: body stretched out nearly horizontal behind the leading leg
frames.50: uppercut: crouched with both fists up in front of the chest — the compression before rising into the blow
frames.51: uppercut, the extended frame: driving upright with one fist high above the head, the other at the chest
frames.52: crouching kick: crouched and turned away, arms drawn tight to the body — the frame before the leg goes out
frames.53: crouching kick, the extended frame: leg extended forward along the ground, body leaning well back
frames.54: ? standing with the feet wide and both hands brought together in front of the chest — the charge of a projectile attack
frames.55: ? the same wide stance with one arm thrust forward, hand open — the release that follows 54
frames.56: ? projectile sprite, not a pose: an elongated bolt of energy with a trailing tail, the largest of the set
frames.57: ? projectile sprite: the same bolt, shorter
frames.58: ? projectile sprite: a small flattened blob of energy — the smallest of the set
frames.59: ? projectile sprite: a long bolt with a bright head, close to 56 in size
frames.60: ? projectile sprite: a round ball of energy, no tail — probably a different attack from the bolts in 56-59
frames.68: impact effect: a compact ball of flame with short spikes around it — an effect sprite, not a pose
frames.69: impact effect: the same burst, larger and breaking up into flames at the bottom — the next step of 68
frames.70: ? impact effect: a thin arc of orange sparks, nothing else — the dying end of 68/69, or a separate small effect
frames.71: ? standing with both forearms crossed high in front of the face, weight on the back foot — a guard, or the wind-up of the swing in 72
frames.72: ? overhead swing: arm coming down with a bright arc trail drawn behind it — the trail marks this as the active frame of an attack
frames.73: ? standing with the lead arm raised high and the fist closed — reads as the recovery of 72
frames.74: hit reaction, light: upright, head snapped back, arms flung out and down. Played alone it IS the light reaction; it is also the first frame of the heavier one, which continues into 75
frames.75: hit reaction, heavy: turned away from the blow, near arm across the face, head dropped — the recoil that follows 74 when the attack is strong enough to need one. Not used alone
frames.76: hit reaction to the stomach / a low blow — doubled forward, head down and forward, arms hanging loose
frames.77: the start of going down: off balance, on the way to the floor. Also reads as a stun, and as the start of taking damage in the air
frames.78: falling after being knocked down — body horizontal in the air, head low, legs trailing high
frames.79: landed: flat on the ground, face down, arms spread
frames.80: getting up, first frame — head and shoulder still down, legs coming back under the body
frames.81: getting up, second frame — on hands and knees with the head low, about to stand

frames.83: kick_from_depth, 2 of 5: halfway in, still dithered and already smaller (59 px). Distance is drawn as scale
frames.84: kick_from_depth, 3 of 5: deep in the screen, solid again and side-on, at its smallest
frames.85: kick_from_depth, 4 of 5: on the way back, halfway, leg already extended into the kick
frames.86: kick_from_depth, 5 of 5: nearly back at full distance, leg still extended — the frame that connects
frames.87: standing in the FOREGROUND, fists up — the pose Goku shoots from, and most likely the frame that carries the step forward. 85 px against the idle's 81, so the plane change is drawn as a slight scale-up
frames.88: the whole body flashed solid white — the flare that starts a ki attack, not a teleport and not a missing sprite
frames.89: arm cocked back to throw a ki bolt
frames.90: the ki bolt leaves the hand
frames.91: hands cupped at the hip, charging the Kamehameha
frames.92: the Kamehameha fires — arms thrust forward, body braced
frames.93: receding, 1 of 4 — the standing pose at 67 px
frames.96: receding, 4 of 4 — 30 px, the far distance reached
frames.97: flashed solid white at far scale — the twin of 88
frames.98: standing far, fists up — the idle of the depth plane
frames.99: far: arm thrown up and forward, batting a ki bolt away
frames.100: ? far, standing with the arms in — either the second frame of the far idle or the neutral the deflects return to
frames.101: far: the other deflect, arm up and across
frames.102: far: pulling the body aside to avoid a blow
frames.104: far: taking a hit, recoiling with the arms up
frames.105: far: taking a hit, doubled over

frames.138: throw, 2 of 3: holding on, body turning into the throw

frames.152: ultimate: the same pose as 151 with the aura stripped off
